claims.text: Local chemical fluctuations in complex concentrated alloys produce spatial variations in stacking-fault or shear-fault energy.
Spatial fault-energy variations create hard atomic motifs that resist or pin dislocation motion.
Local fault-energy fluctuations promote deformation-twin nucleation.
The fluctuating fault-energy landscape is a governing origin of yield strength in concentrated alloys.
The fluctuating fault-energy landscape governs ductility by activating alternative deformation mechanisms.
CrCoNi and related alloys can have a metastable FCC lattice at ambient and cryogenic temperatures, with twinning as a major deformation mechanism.
Changing annealing time or temperature relative to rapid quenching systematically tunes chemical short-range order.
Increasing chemical short-range order increases the amplitude of local fault-energy fluctuations.
Both thermally activated dislocation motion and deformation twinning operate from ambient to cryogenic temperatures at engineering strain rates in the proposed alloy class.
Spatial variability in fault energy raises resistance to dislocation glide and therefore elevates yield strength.
Deformation twinning contributes to enhanced ductility in metastable FCC concentrated alloys.
An annealed state with enhanced short-range order will have a higher yield strength than a rapidly quenched, near-random state of the same alloy.
An annealed state with enhanced short-range order will develop a greater deformation-twinning fraction than a rapidly quenched, near-random state.
A fully homogenized random solid solution has minimal pronounced local variations in stacking-fault energy.
Fault-energy-fluctuation strengthening can dominate strengthening from elastic misfit in complex concentrated alloys.
Grain-size effects or elastic-modulus differences may become significant outside the proposed processing and temperature regimes.
Prolonged annealing enhances short-range order, whereas rapid quenching preserves a near-random chemical distribution.
Observed dislocation-pinning features should correlate with the local fault-energy landscape.

contradictions.description: The cause is described as chemical-disorder-driven, but the intervention and prediction treat increased chemical order as producing larger fault-energy fluctuations. The hypothesis does not reconcile how increasing order strengthens a landscape attributed to disorder.
